name: contract-panel-visual
description: Visual verification of the contract panel UI: available contracts list with material type, quantity, unit price, deadline and penalties; active contracts with progress; completed contract history; accept/reject/negotiate buttons. Accept, the delivery amount and Deliver are all driven through the Contracts panel's own controls (issue #479); only the clock, world setup and the read-only list/status steps remain console commands The Contracts panel is opened once and left open: the tool rail TOGGLES a panel, so re-clicking its entry would close the panel the next step needs.

expect.note: real click on the Contracts panel's first available row -- contract #1 (Supply dirtite) is genuinely first in both the console list and the panel, matching `contract accept 1`'s explicit id; no Finding #55-class mismatch here

steps.description: #513/#581: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id="1"]`, the contract this step's `command` names. Unscoped, `.bs-contract-accept` always resolves to whichever offered card is first in the DOM, so command mode accepted contract #1 literally while interaction mode accepted whatever led the list -- two channels driving different contracts while both reported pass, because nothing asserted here can tell them apart (`activeContractCount` counts accepts, not identities). `level1-win-efficient` is what that costs once a `[data-contract-id]`-scoped assertion is added on top: its guard failed with its control absent from the DOM entirely, red on `main`, cause pointing nowhere near the accept step. ContractsPanel sets `data-contract-id` on offered cards (`makeOfferedCard`), so scoping removes the DOM-order coupling rather than baking around it.

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

role: guard (issue #515): both the amount input and DELIVER button are genuinely disabled here — `amountInput.disabled = maxDeliverable <= 0` and `deliverBtn.disabled = maxDeliverable <= 0` (ContractsPanel.ts) — because this scenario never mines or hauls, so nothing is ever in storage (0.0 kg available).
